output.headline: Ratifies $10,851 contract with North American Fence & Railing for Manzanita child center fencing

money.evidence: in the lump sum amount of $10,851.00

output.summary: North American Fence & Railing, Inc. will replace the old main gate at the Manzanita Child Development Center with a new fence and gate that includes a panic push bar. The lump sum is $10,851, which includes a $1,000 contingency. Work was scheduled for February 5 to February 12, 2025, before this ratification vote.

output.headline: Accepts up to $508,305 from the California Dept. of Food and Agriculture for school food and gardens
output.summary: The district is accepting a state grant of up to $508,305 for "Growing EFG (Environment, Food, and Garden) Programming." It is meant to connect students with healthy local food in cafeterias, gardens and classrooms, buy more local produce and proteins from socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers, and add field trips. The grant covers January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026.

vendor.name: California Department of Food and Agriculture

output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,000 for Curacubby's Attendly software for YES Sports Saturday event check-in
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a services agreement with Curacubby, Inc. to use its Attendly software so families can enroll students in YES Sports Saturday events and check them in and out in a way that meets funding requirements. The district can spend up to $20,000 for February 1 through June 30, 2025. A separate data sharing agreement sets the rules for sharing student data with Curacubby and for protecting it.

output.headline: Pays King Construction Inspection $8,740 for inspector services on the Melrose schoolyard project
schools: Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title refers to the Castlemont High School Solar Battery Plant Storage Project, but the action text describes the Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park Living Schoolyard Project.

The district will pay $8,740. Work is scheduled from March 13 to June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Adds $8,320 and 90 days to Data Media Services' Claremont Middle School camera security contract
output.summary: Change Order No. 1 pays Data Media Services, Inc. up to $8,320 more to upgrade the camera server for the Claremont Middle School Security Improvement Project, raising the contract price from $129,000 to $137,320. It also extends the term by 90 days, through February 25, 2025. It includes approval of preliminary change order 1 (PCO1). The new end date is before this March 12, 2025 vote.

output.headline: Pays Dialog Design $8,800 for added structural engineering at the Melrose Leadership Academy
schools: Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title calls the site the Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park Schoolyard Project, while the action text calls it the Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park Accessibility Project No. 22120.
output.summary: Dialog Design, LP will provide additional structural engineering construction administration services and help the district complete the Division of State Architect (DSA) closeout process for the Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park Accessibility Project. The district will pay $8,800. Work was scheduled to start February 27, 2025, before this vote, and to last until June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Awards Star Elevator up to $824,380 to repair and maintain wheelchair lifts at schools through 2028
output.summary: The Board is awarding a maintenance contract to Star Elevator, Inc., the lowest responsible bidder, to repair and maintain wheelchair lifts at various district sites. The district can spend up to $824,380. Work is expected to start March 13, 2025 and run through June 30, 2028.

output.headline: Adds $88,442 to Jensen Hughes' fire alarm consulting contract for two school projects
output.summary: Amendment No. 8 adds $88,442 for Jensen Hughes, Inc. to provide fire alarm system consulting for the Hintil Kuu Child Development Center Fire and Intrusion Alarm Project ($5,775) and the Coliseum College Preparatory Academy Expansion Project ($82,667). It raises the contract's not-to-exceed amount from $348,520 to $436,962.

output.headline: Approves up to $114,500 for HTF Staffing to cover special education teacher leaves and vacancies
output.summary: HTF Staffing LLC will provide special education teacher services to cover unexpected leaves and vacancies. The district can spend up to $114,500 for February 10 through May 30, 2025, so the service period began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays ER Plumbing & Construction up to $127,665 to replace pipes and fix the kitchen at Allendale Elementary
output.summary: ER Plumbing & Construction will tear up and redo the kitchen floor at Allendale Elementary School, replace lead-based pipes and fittings, install a new grease trap, sinks and faucets, and put in a new gas stove. The district can spend up to $127,665 for work from December 13, 2024 through March 31, 2025, so the work period began before this approval.

output.headline: Awards Data Sync Communications $85,500 to install security cameras at Hillcrest K-8
output.summary: Data Sync Communications, Inc. was the lowest responsible and responsive bidder. It will install 24 new security cameras, repair or adjust five existing cameras, supply four spare cameras, and replace and upgrade the server. The $85,500 includes an $8,000 contingency, and work is expected from March 13 to June 11, 2025.

output.headline: Awards Redgwick Construction $1,347,100 to rebuild play areas and gardens at Madison Primary School
output.summary: The Board is awarding the Madison Primary School site improvements contract to Redgwick Construction Co., the lowest responsible bidder. The work removes old play structures, fencing and surfacing and adds new safety surfacing, drainage, garden beds, irrigation, trees and turf. The $1,347,100 includes a $180,000 contingency allowance, and the work is expected to take 58 days, from March 13 to May 9, 2025.

output.headline: Leases a fiber-optic link between two district sites from Sonic for up to $6,000, through 2030
output.summary: The district would lease a single dark fiber link (an unused fiber-optic cable the district lights itself) from Sonic. The link connects 1011 Union Street and 955 High Street in Oakland. The term is July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2030, with up to $6,000 allowed, subject to the district being awarded E-Rate funding (a federal program that discounts school internet costs). The agreement also has five 1-year renewal options.

output.headline: Adds $163,200 and two years to Sonic's internet service contract, raising it to $408,000
output.summary: This amendment extends the district's internet services agreement with Sonic from June 30, 2025 to June 30, 2027. It adds $163,200, raising the not-to-exceed amount from $244,800 to $408,000 (the district's share). It is paid from E-Rate (a federal program that discounts school internet costs) and the district's utility account. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Pays ACC Environmental up to $12,947 for a hazardous materials survey at Emerson Elementary

money.evidence: in the not to exceed amount of $12,947.00

output.summary: ACC Environmental Consultants will do a hazardous material survey before renovation work on the Emerson Elementary School Intrusion Alarm Replacement Project. The district will pay up to $12,947. Work is scheduled from March 13 to June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost UC Cooperative Extension master gardener partnership for school gardens through 2027
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a no-cost agreement with the Regents of the University of California, through its Alameda County Cooperative Extension Master Gardener Program. Master gardeners will mentor food corps service members and teachers and staff, assess school gardens, lead monthly Saturday talks and community work days, and help grow seedlings. It runs October 1, 2024 through June 30, 2027.

vendor.name: The Regents of the University of California (UC Cooperative Extension Office for Alameda County)

output.headline: Buys up to $433,316 of network equipment from CDW-G through another agency's contract

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $433,316.23

output.summary: The district will buy network infrastructure equipment and services from CDW Government, LLC (CDW-G) for up to $433,316.23 from April 1, 2025 to September 30, 2027. The district is buying through an existing contract of the School Project for Utility Rate Reduction (SPURR) joint powers authority instead of running its own bid. The purchase depends on the district being awarded E-Rate funding.

output.headline: Buys up to $3.92M of technology equipment and services from CDW-G through another agency's contract
output.summary: The district will buy equipment, licensing, services and support from CDW Government, LLC (CDW-G) for up to $3,922,202.73 from April 1, 2025 to September 30, 2027. The district is buying through an existing contract of the School Project for Utility Rate Reduction (SPURR) joint powers authority instead of running its own bid. The purchase depends on the district being awarded E-Rate funding.

output.headline: Buys T-Mobile lines and hotspots via a shared purchasing contract; lines capped at $2,671,704 a year
output.summary: The Board is declaring it is in the district's best interest to buy T-Mobile service through an existing contract that the National Association of State Procurement Officials (NASPO) ValuePoint program set up, instead of running its own bid. It also approves an E-Rate agreement (a federal program that discounts school phone and internet costs). The text lists a yearly cap of $2,671,704 for lines of service and separately $520,800 for hotspot devices, for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2028.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $45,000 for KH Design to lead student and community work on three school murals
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with KH Design to involve students, the community and staff in making three murals at school sites that have not yet been chosen. The district can spend up to $45,000 for March 1 through June 30, 2025. The agreement is handled through the Special Education Department, but the text does not say the murals are tied to special education.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $32,000 for a consultant to support the district's Arts Enrichment Initiative
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with an individual consultant to provide arts-based youth development program support and consultation for the Arts Enrichment Initiative. The district can spend up to $32,000 for February 3 through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Servio Consulting up to $65,625 to move after-school planning and budget tools into Salesforce
output.summary: Servio Consulting, LLC will convert the after-school program planning and budget development processes now done in a tool called Quip into Salesforce screen flows. The goal is to work more efficiently and cut down on manual data entry. The district can spend up to $65,625 for March 13 through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $5,000 to coach the Allendale Elementary principal
output.summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will provide instructional leadership coaching to the principal of Allendale Elementary School to support the principal's role and development. The district can spend up to $5,000 for February 3 through May 16, 2025, so the service period began before this approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $11,050 for Kendall Hunt's two-day training on the Illustrative Mathematics curriculum
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with Kendall Hunt Publishers for a two-day foundational training on Illustrative Mathematics, the district's adopted math curriculum. The district can spend up to $11,050. The service dates were August 1 and 2, 2024, before this approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for Woodbury Education Consulting to coach high school math teachers
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with Woodbury Education Consulting Inc. to support high school math team leads. The work includes planning meetings, co-leading Professional Learning Community meetings, and coaching teachers on using Math Language Routines to support student-to-student talk. The district can spend up to $15,000 for February 3 through May 23, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Hope Reimagined up to $12,000 for clinical supervision and staff training at Hillcrest Elementary
output.summary: Hope Reimagined will provide clinical supervision, staff training and support in addressing social-emotional, behavioral and academic problems at Hillcrest Elementary School. The district can spend up to $12,000 for February 1 through May 30, 2025, so the service period began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $8,538.75 for lunchtime supervision at Hillcrest Elementary
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will provide lunchtime supervision at Hillcrest Elementary School. Its staff will lead group activities and help students learn conflict resolution skills. The district can spend up to $8,538.75 for August 12, 2024 through May 28, 2025, so the service period began before this approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Lend A Hand Foundation to provide supplies and clothing for McKinney-Vento students
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with Lend A Hand Foundation to give the district's McKinney-Vento Program school supplies, hygiene kits, clothing, snacks and other resources students need for school. The district can spend up to $5,000 for December 2, 2024 through May 30, 2025. The funding source is listed as Homeless Children & Youth.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $114,000 for Brigaid to develop recipes and train Central Kitchen staff
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with Brigaid LLC to help the Nutrition Services menu planner develop and test recipes, including summer and 2025-26 school year menus. Brigaid will also support scratch cooking and staff training at the Central Kitchen. The district can spend up to $114,000 for January 1 through June 30, 2025.

The district is buying through an existing contract of the School Project for Utility Rate Reduction (SPURR) joint powers authority instead of running its own bid. The purchase depends on the district being awarded E-Rate funding.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for a consultant to prepare Nutrition Services for a spring review and audit
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a short agreement with an individual consultant to help Nutrition Services prepare for its spring administrative review and audit. The work covers staffing and operating plans, second chance breakfast, central kitchen operations and written procedures. The district can spend up to $15,000 for February 8 through March 5, 2025.

output.headline: Sets up a no-cost teacher intern and student-teaching partnership with Academy of Art University
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Academy of Art University sets up an intern program and a fieldwork program for people earning K-12 teaching credentials, including art education. It runs July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2030 and costs the district nothing beyond pay for teacher interns, who are district employees.

output.headline: Sets up a no-cost fieldwork placement partnership with University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) lets graduate students from the University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences do fieldwork in district placements, including for pupil personnel services credentials. It runs January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2029 and costs the district nothing, except that some non-employee interns may receive stipends paid from nonprofit grants to the district, such as from the Ed Fund.

vendor.name: University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences

output.headline: Pays Elevate Oakland up to $1,000 for a disability-awareness puppet show at Montclair Elementary
output.summary: Elevate Oakland will put on a puppet show at Montclair Elementary School for Disability Awareness month. Students will learn the history of disability rights and how puppets are made, as part of an arts project. The district can spend up to $1,000 for January 27 and 28, 2025, which are dates before this approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,500 for Swanson & Cosgrave to assist ten charter high school career pathways
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an agreement with Swanson & Cosgrave Consulting LLC to give technical help to ten charter schools that receive Measure N and Measure H funding. The consultant will help line up their high school pathways with the 2023-26 Linked Learning Quality Standards. The district can spend up to $10,500 for January 27 through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Oakland Symphony partnership for instrument lessons at United for Success Academy
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a no-cost agreement with Oakland Symphony. Symphony musicians will work with a small group of students during their regular music class and with their music teacher, helping them learn a string or band instrument. It covers January 27 through June 30, 2025 at United for Success Academy.

output.headline: Adds $6,000 to a contract for English classes for families at Elmhurst United Middle School
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, an amendment that adds $6,000 to an individual contractor's agreement, raising the not-to-exceed amount from $6,000 to $12,000. The contractor continues to develop English language lessons and teach weekly English classes to students' families at Elmhurst United Middle School. The term does not change: January 21 through May 22, 2025.

output.headline: Accepts a $7,500 grant for career-pathway field trips at Castlemont High School
output.summary: The district is accepting a $7,500 grant from the Bay Area K-16 Collaborative College & Career Exploration Fund, whose fiscal agent is UC Berkeley. The money will pay for field trips with pathway-specific activities for students and educators in the Education, Health Care and Engineering/STEM pathways at Castlemont High School. The grant period is October 1, 2024 through May 31, 2025.

vendor.name: Bay Area K-16 Collaborative College & Career Exploration Fund

output.headline: Accepts a $7,500 grant for college and career field trips at McClymonds High School
output.summary: The Bay Area K-16 Collaborative College & Career Exploration Fund, which is managed by UC Berkeley, is giving the district $7,500. The money pays for field trips to four-year universities (CSU and UC) with activities tied to the Education, Health Care, and Engineering/STEM pathways at McClymonds High School. It covers October 1, 2024 through May 31, 2025.

vendor.name: Bay Area K-16 Collaborative College & Career Exploration Fund

output.headline: Amends Oakland Promise data-sharing agreement to add student-level economic data at no cost
output.summary: The district will give Oakland Promise additional student-level data on Socio Economic Disadvantaged (SED) status, alongside the data it already shares, including National Student Clearinghouse (NSC) data. The data is shared through the High School Linked Learning Office. The agreement's term does not change (January 28, 2021 through October 31, 2026), and no money is involved.

output.headline: Approves the 2025-26 funding application for the state General Child Care program
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution approving the district's continued funding application to the California Department of Social Services for the California General Child Care Program (CCTR). The program is run by the Early Childhood Education Department. It covers July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, and the text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Civic Productions' arts work with Oakland High students

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: The district pays Civic Productions LLC up to $5,000 to help with the Autumn Lights Festival event and installation, talk with tenth-grade Visual Arts & Academics Magnet Program (VAAMP) students about careers and summer internships, show student artwork at Clinton Park, and begin planning student murals. The term runs August 12, 2024 through May 22, 2025. The board is ratifying the agreement after the term began.

output.headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $13,860 for newcomer student support at Oakland High

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $13,860.00

output.summary: Soccer Without Borders will run learning circles that encourage social and emotional learning and hold one-on-one check-ins for Newcomer students at Oakland High School. The district will pay up to $13,860. The term runs August 12, 2024 through May 30, 2025.

output.headline: Declares district vehicles surplus and authorizes their disposal
output.summary: Resolution No. 2425-0134 declares certain district-owned vehicles obsolete and surplus and allows the district to dispose of them. The text does not list the vehicles, say how they will be disposed of, or state any dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies reappointment of four members to the Measure G parcel tax oversight committee
output.summary: The board ratifies the Board President's reappointment of four members, each starting a second term, to the Measure G Parcel Tax Independent Citizens Oversight Committee. Each has satisfactorily served a first term. The new term runs February 1, 2025 through January 31, 2027.

output.headline: Approves Skyline High trip for 3 seniors and 1 adult to visit Atlanta's historically Black colleges
output.summary: The board authorizes three 12th grade Skyline High School students and one adult to travel to Atlanta, Georgia, to visit Historically Black Colleges and Universities and historical landmarks. The trip runs April 7 through April 13, 2025. The text does not state a cost; the listed funding source is General Funds.

output.headline: Approves Fremont High trip for 21 students and 4 adults to visit Washington, DC
output.summary: The board authorizes twenty-one students in grades 9 through 12 and four adults from Fremont High School to travel to Washington, DC. The trip runs March 23 through March 27, 2025. The text does not state a cost.

output.headline: Approves Castlemont High Pacific Bridge Club trip to Jakarta, Indonesia, listed as no fiscal impact
output.summary: The board authorizes sixteen students in grades 9 through 12 from the Pacific Bridge Club at Castlemont High School and four adults to travel to Jakarta, Indonesia. The trip runs March 20 through April 3, 2025. The item lists no fiscal impact to the district.
